name: Application layer
what_it_is: The software and workflows that pay the $1.00. The chart begins at the model user, so the layer that generates the demand is not drawn at all.
exposure_verdict: Absent from the exhibit and absent from our universe. If cheaper tokens are an input-cost decline, this is the layer that banks it.
key_risk: Cannot be sized from this exhibit. The omission may be the most important thing in it.

name: External funding
what_it_is: 17.3 cents of investor capital entering alongside every $1.00 of customer spend, because the model layer loses money.
value_capture: Negative. This is subsidy entering the chain.
exposure_verdict: Not investable. Tracked because it is the chain's least durable input: roughly 15% of all flow is funding rather than revenue.
weekly_metric: private AI funding announcements and hyperscaler capex guidance
key_risk: If funding tightens the chain contracts from the order-placing layer downward, not evenly.

name: Foundation models
what_it_is: The labs. Take in $1.173 and book no profit box on the exhibit.
value_capture: None on this estimate. The layer closest to the intelligence captures the least.
exposure_verdict: Zero coverage. Mostly private, so the gap is partly structural rather than a choice.
weekly_metric: token price benchmarks and published pricing changes
key_risk: Open-weight competition compresses this layer first, and it is the layer everything downstream is ordered against.

name: Hyperscaler cloud
what_it_is: Cloud platforms monetising AI simultaneously through infrastructure, their own models, their own silicon and enterprise relationships.
value_capture: 29.7 cents — the largest single slice by a wide margin.
exposure_verdict: ZERO NAMES. Half of all identified profit in the chain sits in a layer we do not track. This has never been decided on purpose.
weekly_metric: aggregate capex guidance and cloud segment growth
key_risk: Concentration. Four buyers set the order book for every layer below them.

name: Pure neocloud
what_it_is: GPU capacity rented without owning the customer, the model, the silicon or the balance sheet.
exposure_verdict: Zero names, and on this estimate that is the correct answer rather than a gap.
weekly_metric: listed neocloud gross margin and contract duration disclosures
key_risk: The 0.2c figure is the cheapest claim in the exhibit to verify against filings and the most damaging to the exhibit if wrong.

name: Data-centre chips and servers
what_it_is: Routing bucket. Splits into commercial chips, custom ASICs, memory, foundry, server OEM and other OEM cost of goods.
value_capture: Pass-through. Profit is taken by its children.

name: Commercial chips
what_it_is: Merchant accelerator and networking silicon sold to anyone who will buy it.
exposure_verdict: Adjacent, not core. We hold interconnect and custom-silicon names, none of the merchant accelerator profit pool that the 13.0c actually describes.
weekly_metric: revenue growth and gross margin from weekly_metrics
key_risk: Our four names are exposed to the same aggregate compute demand but capture a different, smaller pool than the one this cent figure measures.

name: Custom chips (ASICs)
what_it_is: Accelerators designed to a single buyer's specification.
value_capture: 1.1 cents. The smallest silicon slice despite being the loudest narrative.
exposure_verdict: Covered. Note the asymmetry the narrative misses: ASICs taking share from merchant silicon moves value from a 13.0c pool into a 1.1c pool.
key_risk: A share shift into this layer shrinks the total profit pool rather than relocating it.

name: Memory
what_it_is: HBM and conventional DRAM. Content per rack is claimed to be rising.
value_capture: 5.8 cents — larger than foundry and server OEM combined.
exposure_verdict: ZERO NAMES. Third-largest profit box in the chain and we track none of it.
key_risk: Historically the most cyclical layer in semiconductors. Absence may be defensible; it has not been argued.

name: Foundry
what_it_is: Leading-edge wafer manufacture and advanced packaging.
exposure_verdict: Zero names. A single-supplier chokepoint for the entire chain and it is untracked.
key_risk: Geopolitical concentration is the chain's largest single point of failure and sits entirely outside our coverage.

name: Server OEM and ODM
what_it_is: Assembly of accelerators, memory and networking into racks.
value_capture: 2.8 cents on a very large revenue base — a thin-margin integration business.
exposure_verdict: One name. Correctly sized: high revenue, low profit share.
key_risk: Margin is set by component pricing the layer does not control.

name: Other OEM cost of goods
what_it_is: Remaining bill of materials with no profit box drawn.

name: Data-centre equipment and facility
what_it_is: Routing bucket. Splits into equipment profit, construction spending, energy spending and leased/colo spending.
value_capture: Pass-through. Only the first child has a profit box.

name: Equipment — power, cooling and networking
what_it_is: Power distribution, thermal management and networking inside the data hall.
exposure_verdict: Our single deepest layer. Sixteen names competing for 3.8 cents of every AI dollar.
weekly_metric: aggregate market cap and median revenue growth from weekly_metrics
key_risk: The layer we know best is worth a quarter of what the layer we do not track is worth. This is the central finding of the mapping.

name: Construction spending
what_it_is: Engineering, procurement and construction of the buildings and their electrical works.
value_capture: No profit box. Routed out of frame as spending.
exposure_verdict: Three names in a flow the exhibit declines to credit with AI profit. The trained-labour moat argued in the electricity note is invisible to this lens.
key_risk: Either the exhibit understates a real moat, or we are underwriting a cost line as though it were a profit pool.

name: Energy spending
what_it_is: Electricity purchased to run the load, flowing to generators and utilities.
value_capture: No profit box. Routed out of frame as spending.
exposure_verdict: Nineteen names — our largest single concentration — in the flow the exhibit treats purely as cost. GE Vernova and the fuel-cycle names sit a further step beyond the frame entirely, selling to the recipients of this spending.
weekly_metric: aggregate market cap and realised power price proxies
key_risk: The scarcity rent argued in research/themes/age-of-electricity.md is real but has no box on this chart. Both statements need to survive together or one of them is wrong.

name: Leased and colocation spending
what_it_is: Rent paid to third-party data-centre landlords.
value_capture: No profit box. Routed out of frame as spending.
exposure_verdict: Zero names. A long-lease, contracted-cash-flow layer that the store has never assessed.
key_risk: Excluded from the exhibit's profit attribution despite being one of the more contractually durable positions in the chain.
